issues.detail: The Hebrew 'רִבֹּתַ֣יִם אַלְפֵ֣י שִׁנְאָ֑ן' means 'twice ten thousand, thousands of Shinan' (i.e., 'myriads, thousands of Shinan' – Shinan is a place name, likely referring to Sinai or a region). The Chinese renders 'אַלְפֵ֣י שִׁנְאָ֑ן' as '千個天使長' (thousands of archangels), adding '天使長' (archangels) which is not in the Hebrew, and misidentifies 'שִׁנְאָ֑ן' as a number/description rather than a proper name. This changes the meaning: the Hebrew speaks of myriads and thousands of Shinan (a place), not of archangels.

The Hebrew 'שִׁנְאָ֑ן' (Shinan) is a proper place name, but the Chinese translates it as part of a phrase '千個天使長' (thousands of archangels), effectively dropping the place name and substituting a different concept.
